skill.displayName: 标前分析助手-投标前必查的一份报告

llm.summary: This skill appears to support bid analysis, but it deserves Review because it can create and store account credentials, collect a device-derived identifier, and place signed access links into shareable reports.

dimensions.detail: Network access is mostly scoped to the vendor domains and user-provided bid data, but auto-registration transmits platform, CPU architecture, and a MAC-derived hash, and report generation preserves signed sk URLs in local/shareable HTML without a clear warning that those links may grant access.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No dependency installer or remote code loader was found. Metadata requires ZLBX_API_KEY, while optional runtime onboarding can create ~/.zlbx/config.json if the user consents.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation is broad for pre-bid research and the skill defaults to a 12-25 call workflow after a cost notice. Several operational request-identity and update-ack instructions are duplicated inside HTML-comment blocks; much of the behavior is also disclosed elsewhere, but the comment-wrapped form makes review and user awareness weaker.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill can read credentials from the environment or ~/.zlbx/config.json and persist newly issued API keys under ~/.zlbx/config.json. It does not install services or background agents, but persistent secrets and auto-login/recharge links are high-impact account state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core bid-analysis workflow and HTML report renderer fit the stated purpose, but the package also includes account auto-registration, recharge/login-link handling, persistent credential storage, and mandatory use of signed access URLs in reports, which materially expands the user impact beyond analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable using this vendor's procurement API, allowing the skill to read or store a ZLBX API key, and potentially creating a trial account tied to a hashed device identifier. Treat generated sk and auto-login links as sensitive: avoid sharing reports or screenshots containing those URLs unless you intend recipients to have access.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: Downgraded: render_report.py is an export helper, not the whole skill; the markdown artifacts define the actual bid-analysis API workflow.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scope concern: mandatory activation for broadly described pre-bid investigation can cause costly or unnecessary external queries.
[AE1] expected: Overridden: the referenced render_report.py file was locally present and inspected; it is a self-contained HTML renderer.
[P2] unexpected: Accepted in part: request headers are expected for an API integration, but placing repeated operational instructions and display-ack behavior inside HTML-comment blocks is under-transparent.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: automatic account enrollment, local credential persistence, login, and recharge flows are adjacent to but broader than bid analysis.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Accepted: collecting a MAC-derived hash is disclosed and consent-gated, but it is still a persistent device identifier for a trial-account flow.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted: the artifacts require preserving sk signed URLs in conversation output and shareable HTML reports without clearly warning users that these links are sensitive.
[SC3] expected: Overridden: the base64 content is an embedded PNG logo used as an image source; no decoding-and-execution path was found.
[LP3] expected: Report file creation is expected and disclosed, but the lack of an explicit tool/path permission boundary supports the broader Review posture.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese-language prompts are consistent with the China-focused procurement product and are not a material security issue here.
[E1] unexpected: Accepted in part: external registration calls are disclosed and consent-gated, but they transmit locally derived device features to a vendor service.
[RA2] unexpected: Accepted as a Review concern: durable API-key storage in ~/.zlbx/config.json is documented but increases cross-session credential exposure.
